apollo-11-site.name: Apollo 11 Landing Site

locations.label: Eagle LM Descent Stage, Mare Tranquillitatis

apollo-11-site.summary: Apollo 11 was the first crewed mission to touch down on the Moon.
apollo-11-site.hook: I carried humanity to the lunar surface and my descent stage still stands in Tranquility Base.
apollo-11-site.how_it_worked: The Eagle descent stage used a throttleable descent engine and four landing pads to achieve the first powered lunar landing.
apollo-11-site.science: Astronauts collected 21.5 kilograms of lunar rocks and deployed early passive seismometers.

facts.text: The descent stage served as the launch pad when the ascent stage lifted off to rejoin orbit.
Laser pulses from Earth are still reflected off mirror prisms placed at the site.

image.alt: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle resting on the lunar surface at Tranquility Base, with Buzz Aldrin preparing to deploy experiments

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Mare Tranquillitatis descent stage visual contact confirmed.
Tranquility Base: the first location on another celestial body visited by humans.
The throttleable descent engine fired continuously to guide the Eagle past boulder fields.
Returned 21.5 kilograms of ancient lunar basalt and breccia dating back 3.7 billion years.
The steel commemorative plaque remains attached to the ladder strut.
Resting permanently at 0.67408° N, 23.47297° E.

apollo-12-site.name: Apollo 12 Landing Site

locations.label: Intrepid LM Descent Stage, Oceanus Procellarum

apollo-12-site.summary: Apollo 12 demonstrated precision pinpoint landing on another celestial body.
apollo-12-site.hook: I landed within 200 meters of Surveyor 3 to prove pinpoint lunar landing accuracy.
apollo-12-site.how_it_worked: Achieved precision landing using radar updates and deployed an ALSEP science station powered by an RTG.
apollo-12-site.science: Recorded eight years of continuous seismic and solar wind data using its nuclear-powered station.

facts.text: Astronauts walked over to the robotic Surveyor 3 lander and inspected parts exposed to vacuum for over two years.
Left a SNAP-27 radioisotope thermoelectric generator on the Moon that transmitted data until 1977.

image.alt: Astronaut Alan Bean works at the equipment stowage bay of the Apollo 12 Lunar Module

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Pinpoint landing zone in Oceanus Procellarum located.
Apollo 12 demonstrated precision landing within walking distance of Surveyor 3.
Automated Doppler radar descent navigation enabled touchdown within 180 meters of target.
Retrieved components from Surveyor 3 to analyze long-term cosmic radiation exposure.
Astronauts Conrad and Bean deployed the first full ALSEP scientific station.
Intrepid descent stage located at 3.01239° S, 23.42157° W.

apollo-15-lrv.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle
apollo-15-lrv.summary: The Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle was the first motorized vehicle driven on the Moon.
apollo-15-lrv.hook: I was the first rover driven on the Moon and traveled over 27 kilometers across Hadley Rille.
apollo-15-lrv.how_it_worked: Powered by non-rechargeable silver-zinc batteries and four electric wheel motors with wire-mesh tires.
apollo-15-lrv.science: Allowed astronauts to travel far from the lander and retrieve the 4-billion-year-old Genesis Rock.

facts.text: The rover was parked about 160 meters from the Lunar Module so its camera could film liftoff.
Its tires were made of woven zinc-coated piano wire with titanium chevrons for grip.

image.alt: Astronaut James Irwin works at the Lunar Roving Vehicle at Hadley-Apennine, with Mount Hadley behind

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Lunar Roving Vehicle 1 stationed near Hadley Rille.
The first motorized vehicle driven by humans on the surface of another world.
Powered by four 0.25-horsepower electric motors with woven wire mesh wheels.
Allowed crew to traverse 27.9 kilometers to sample the deep layered gorge of Hadley Rille.
The commemorative Fallen Astronaut memorial figurine rests nearby in the regolith.

apollo-17-site.name: Apollo 17 Landing Site
apollo-17-site.summary: Apollo 17 was the final Apollo mission to land astronauts on the Moon.
apollo-17-site.hook: I was the final Apollo human landing site in the Taurus-Littrow valley in 1972.
apollo-17-site.how_it_worked: Supported the longest human stay on the lunar surface: over 74 hours with three moonwalks.
apollo-17-site.science: Discovered orange soil beads formed by ancient volcanic fire-fountain eruptions on the Moon.

facts.text: Harrison Schmitt, the Lunar Module Pilot on Apollo 17, was the first professional geologist on the Moon.
The crew traveled over 35 kilometers in their rover and gathered 110 kg of soil and rock samples.

image.alt: Harrison Schmitt beside the flag at Taurus-Littrow, with the Lunar Module and Lunar Roving Vehicle in the background

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Taurus-Littrow valley final Apollo landing site.
The culminating crewed lunar mission of the 20th century in December 1972.
Geologist-astronaut Harrison Schmitt and Gene Cernan lived on the lunar surface for 75 hours.
Discovered orange volcanic pyroclastic glass beads formed by lunar explosive volcanism.
Returned 110.5 kilograms of samples, the largest collection from any lunar expedition.
Challenger descent stage coordinates: 20.1908° N, 30.77168° E.

apollo-retroreflectors.name: Apollo Laser Retroreflectors
apollo-retroreflectors.summary: Laser ranging retroreflectors are optical prism arrays still used for research today.
apollo-retroreflectors.hook: I require zero power and scientists on Earth still bounce laser beams off my prisms.
apollo-retroreflectors.how_it_worked: Corner-cube fused-silica prisms reflect incident laser pulses back toward their precise origin on Earth.
apollo-retroreflectors.science: Confirmed that the Moon is spiraling away from Earth at a rate of 3.8 centimeters per year.

facts.text: These retroreflectors are the only Apollo surface experiments still in active operational scientific use.
The Apollo 15 reflector array contains 300 corner cubes, three times larger than Apollo 11.

image.alt: Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retro-Reflector and seismic experiment deployed on the lunar surface, seen from the Lunar Module

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Passive optical array detected in Mare Tranquillitatis.
High-precision silica corner-cube prisms that require zero electrical power.
Telescopes on Earth fire laser pulses; these retroreflectors bounce them back directly.
Measures the Earth-Moon distance to millimeter accuracy, tracking the Moon drifting 3.8 cm/year.
Three Apollo arrays (11, 14, 15) remain active scientific instruments today.
Operating across Mare Tranquillitatis, Fra Mauro, and Hadley-Apennine.

blue-ghost-1.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
blue-ghost-1.summary: Blue Ghost Mission 1 was a commercial lunar lander flying payloads for NASA.
blue-ghost-1.hook: I delivered ten NASA payloads to Mare Crisium under the Commercial Lunar Payload Services initiative.
blue-ghost-1.how_it_worked: Used autonomous thruster guidance to land in Mare Crisium and powered science instruments through the lunar day.
blue-ghost-1.science: Investigated lunar regolith characteristics and tested GPS signal reception at lunar distance.

facts.text: Blue Ghost was selected under NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services to deliver science payloads.
Completed operations across a full 14-day lunar daylight period in Mare Crisium.

image.alt: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying Firefly Aerospace Blue Ghost Mission 1 at Launch Complex 39A before launch to the Moon

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Commercial Lunar Payload Services landing site in Mare Crisium.
Commercial lander carrying ten NASA science and technology demonstration instruments.
Equipped with autonomous terrain relative navigation and sample collection mechanisms.
Studies solar wind interactions, lunar regolith plume levitation, and GNSS reception.
Part of NASA Artemis program initiative for regular commercial lunar delivery.
Located in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille at 18.562° N, 61.81° E.

im-1-odysseus.name: IM-1 Odysseus

locations.label: Near Malapert A, Lunar South Polar Region

im-1-odysseus.summary: IM-1 Odysseus achieved the first American commercial soft landing on the Moon.
im-1-odysseus.hook: I touched down near the lunar south pole in 2024 under NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services.
im-1-odysseus.how_it_worked: Used liquid methane and liquid oxygen propulsion along with NASA Doppler Lidar sensor guidance.
im-1-odysseus.science: Demonstrated precision landing sensors and captured radio astronomy measurements in the south polar region.

facts.text: Landed at roughly 80 degrees South, the southernmost point reached by an operational lunar lander at the time.
Carried a retroreflector instrument for future precision navigation around the Moon.

image.alt: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off at night from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39A, carrying the Intuitive Machines Nova-C lander Odysseus for the IM-1 mission

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Nova-C class lander positioned near Malapert A crater.
The first commercial spacecraft to achieve a soft touchdown on the Moon.
Powered by liquid methane and liquid oxygen, navigated via backup NASA optical Doppler lidar.
Gathered radio-frequency plasma measurements and space weather data near the lunar south pole.
Demonstrated commercial deep-space payload delivery in polar cryogenic terrain.
Positioned at 80.13° S, 1.44° E in the lunar south polar region.

surveyor-3.name: Surveyor 3
surveyor-3.summary: Surveyor 3 was an unmanned robotic probe that dug the first trenches in lunar soil.
surveyor-3.hook: I landed in 1967 in Oceanus Procellarum and was later visited by Apollo 12 astronauts.
surveyor-3.how_it_worked: Used radar Doppler landing guidance, a surface soil scoop arm, and a television transmission system.
surveyor-3.science: Proved the lunar soil could physically support the weight of heavy Apollo Lunar Modules.

facts.text: Apollo 12 landed within walking distance in 1969 and brought Surveyor 3 camera parts home to Earth.
Returned 6,315 television images during its first lunar day of surface operation.

image.alt: Surveyor 3 in its crater with the Apollo 12 Lunar Module on the horizon

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Imaging first robotic footprint in Oceanus Procellarum.
Before astronauts walked here, Surveyor tested if the lunar dust would hold weight.
Its robotic scoop dug trenches into the regolith to calculate surface bearing strength.
Data confirmed the soil could support human landing modules without sinking.
Primary NASA records confirm Apollo 12 retrieved its camera two years later.
Coordinates verified inside Surveyor Crater at 3.015° S, 23.418° W.

curiosity.name: Curiosity Rover (Mars Science Laboratory)
curiosity.summary: Curiosity is a car-sized nuclear-powered rover exploring the geology of Gale Crater.
curiosity.hook: I have climbed Mount Sharp inside Gale Crater since 2012 investigating past habitable environments.
curiosity.how_it_worked: Landed via sky-crane rocket system and runs on an RTG nuclear generator with laser spectrometers and sample drills.
curiosity.science: Discovered ancient organic molecules and evidence that fresh lake water once persisted in Gale Crater.

facts.text: Curiosity has driven over 30 kilometers across Gale Crater and continues active science operations.
Uses its ChemCam instrument to vaporize rock samples with laser pulses from up to 7 meters away.

image.alt: Curiosity rover self-portrait taken with its arm camera at Rocknest in Gale Crater

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Active Mars Science Laboratory telemetry at Gale Crater.
Car-sized nuclear-powered mobile laboratory actively ascending Mount Sharp since 2012.
Powered by a Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator with a 2-meter robotic arm.
Discovered ancient freshwater lake environments containing organic carbon building blocks.
Has driven over 32 kilometers while drilling rock samples and monitoring radiation.
Bradbury Landing coordinates: 4.5895° S, 137.4417° E.

ingenuity.name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
ingenuity.summary: Ingenuity was the first aircraft to achieve powered controlled flight on another planet.
ingenuity.hook: I completed 72 powered flights in the thin atmosphere of Mars before retiring in Jezero Crater.
ingenuity.how_it_worked: Coaxial counter-rotating carbon-fiber rotors spinning at 2,400 RPM to lift in atmospheric density under 1% of Earth.
ingenuity.science: Proved aerial scout capability across complex dunes and guided routes for the Perseverance rover.

facts.text: Originally designed for five demonstration flights, Ingenuity flew 72 times and logged over two hours in the air.
Carried a small swatch of fabric from the Wright brothers 1903 Flyer underneath its solar panel.

image.alt: Close-up of the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter on the Martian surface, taken by the Mastcam-Z cameras on the Perseverance rover

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Valinor Hills final airfield Chi in Jezero Crater.
The first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight in the atmosphere of another world.
Twin counter-rotating carbon-fiber rotors spinning at 2,400+ RPM in thin atmospheric density.
Demonstrated aerial scouting across 72 flights, covering 17 kilometers of Martian terrain.
Carried a swatch of muslin fabric from the Wright Brothers 1903 Flyer.
Airfield Chi coordinates: 18.44° N, 77.45° E.

insight.name: InSight Mars Lander
insight.summary: InSight studied the interior structure of Mars by measuring seismic tremors.
insight.hook: I placed a seismometer on the Martian plains to record marsquakes and map the planet interior.
insight.how_it_worked: Stationary geophysical lander carrying an ultra-sensitive seismometer protected by a wind and thermal shield.
insight.science: Recorded over 1,300 marsquakes, revealing the thickness of Mars crust and the size of its liquid core.

facts.text: InSight recorded a magnitude 5 marsquake in May 2022, the strongest ever detected on another planet.
Dust accumulation on its solar panels steadily reduced power until transmission ceased in late 2022.

image.alt: InSight lander selfie showing its solar panels and deck on Mars

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Elysium Planitia geophysical station.
Dedicated interior exploration lander operating from 2018 through 2022.
Deployed the SEIS ultra-sensitive seismometer under a vacuum-sealed wind and thermal shield.
Detected more than 1,300 marsquakes, revealing the thickness of Mars crust and molten core.
Completed the first comprehensive internal structural mapping of a terrestrial planet.
Homestead Hollow coordinates: 4.5024° N, 135.6234° E.

mars-polar-lander.name: Mars Polar Lander

locations.label: Ultimi Scopuli, South Polar Layered Terrain

mars-polar-lander.summary: Mars Polar Lander was an ambitious robotic probe sent to study the Martian south pole.
mars-polar-lander.hook: Contact was lost during my atmospheric descent into the southern polar terrain of Mars in 1999.
mars-polar-lander.how_it_worked: Designed to use thrusters to touch down softly on layered polar deposits and analyze soil ice.
mars-polar-lander.science: Highlighted the critical need for continuous telemetry during off-world atmospheric descent and landing.

facts.text: Telemetry was lost seconds before atmospheric entry, leading NASA to redesign landing monitoring for all future missions.
Carried two microprobes designed to penetrate the surface soil upon high-speed impact.

image.alt: Mars Polar Lander awaiting testing at Kennedy Space Center before launch

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Southern polar layered deposits wreckage zone.
Intended to investigate water ice and climate history near the south polar cap in 1999.
Designed with descent thrusters, a meteorological station, and a deep-soil scoop.
Telemetry ceased during atmospheric entry due to premature engine cutoff prior to touchdown.
Failure investigations led to modernized entry, descent, and landing telemetry protocols.
Targeted touchdown zone: 76.57° S, 165.2° E.

perseverance-landing-hardware.name: Perseverance Landing Hardware

locations.label: Octavia E. Butler Landing Debris Field, Jezero Crater

perseverance-landing-hardware.summary: The parachute and backshell that protected the Perseverance rover during atmospheric entry.
perseverance-landing-hardware.hook: My parachute and backshell brought Perseverance to Jezero Crater and were later photographed by Ingenuity.
perseverance-landing-hardware.how_it_worked: A supersonic nylon parachute and protective aeroshell slowed the entry vehicle from orbital velocities.
perseverance-landing-hardware.science: Provided valuable engineering data on high-speed entry parachute dynamics in the thin Martian atmosphere.

facts.text: The 70-foot supersonic parachute carried a coded binary pattern spelling Dare Mighty Things in its canopy.
The debris field was imaged from an aerial vantage point by the Ingenuity helicopter during Flight 26.

image.alt: Debris field of the Perseverance backshell and parachute photographed from the air by Ingenuity

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Octavia E. Butler Landing debris field located.
The supersonic parachute and rocket-powered Sky Crane descent stage for Perseverance.
Terrain Relative Navigation guided the descent vehicle away from hazardous cliff faces.
Enabled the pinpoint touchdown of the 1,025-kilogram rover inside ancient Jezero Crater.
Hardware debris field was later surveyed and photographed aerially by Ingenuity.
Jezero Crater field coordinates: 18.4447° N, 77.4508° E.

phoenix.name: Phoenix Mars Lander
phoenix.summary: Phoenix landed in the Martian arctic to study water ice beneath the surface soil.
phoenix.hook: I dug into the arctic soils of northern Mars and verified subsurface water ice in 2008.
phoenix.how_it_worked: Stationary lander equipped with a 2.35-meter robotic trenching arm and thermal oven analyzers.
phoenix.science: Exposed chunks of bright white water ice that sublimated into vapor over several days.

facts.text: Phoenix detected perchlorate salts in the soil, which lower the freezing point of water.
Mission ended when solar panels lost sunlight during the onset of the deep northern Martian winter.

image.alt: Phoenix lander self-portrait on Mars, showing its deck and solar panels from above

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Vastitas Borealis arctic plains landing site.
Stationary lander deployed to investigate the history of water in the Martian arctic.
Used a 2.35-meter robotic trenching arm and Thermal and Evolved-Gas Analyzer ovens.
Exposed and photographed subsurface water ice that sublimated into the atmosphere.
Detected perchlorate salts and calcium carbonate in the alkaline northern soil.
Green Valley touchdown coordinates: 68.22° N, 125.75° W.

sojourner-pathfinder.name: Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner

locations.label: Carl Sagan Memorial Station, Ares Vallis

sojourner-pathfinder.summary: Mars Pathfinder landed the first wheeled rover ever operated on Mars.
sojourner-pathfinder.hook: I carried the microwave-sized Sojourner rover across the ancient floodplains of Ares Vallis.
sojourner-pathfinder.how_it_worked: Used an innovative parachute, retro-rocket, and airbag bounce-landing system on the Martian surface.
sojourner-pathfinder.science: Determined that rocks in Ares Vallis were rounded and sorted by catastrophic prehistoric water floods.

facts.text: The Sojourner microrover weighed only 10.6 kg and operated for nearly three months.
Pathfinder returned 16,500 images and 8.5 million measurements of atmospheric pressure and temperature.

image.alt: Mars Pathfinder lander on the surface of Mars

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Carl Sagan Memorial Station located in Ares Vallis.
Humanity first mobile rover on Mars: the 11.5 kg, six-wheeled Sojourner.
Used airbag cluster cushioning for landing and solar array panels for surface power.
Traveled 100 meters analyzing volcanic boulders using an Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer.
Proved that rover exploration of planetary surfaces was scientifically feasible and robust.
Landed in Ares Vallis outflow channel at 19.47° N, 33.25° W.

spirit-opportunity.name: Spirit and Opportunity

locations.label: Spirit (MER-A), Columbia Memorial Station, Gusev Crater
Opportunity (MER-B), Challenger Memorial Station, Meridiani Planum

spirit-opportunity.summary: Twin robotic rovers searched opposite sides of Mars for evidence of ancient liquid water.
spirit-opportunity.hook: We were twin rovers built for 90 days that explored Mars for over fourteen years.
spirit-opportunity.how_it_worked: Six-wheel rocker-bogie rovers equipped with panoramic cameras, mineral spectrometers, and rock abrasion tools.
spirit-opportunity.science: Discovered hematite blueberries and silica deposits proving liquid water once covered ancient Martian terrain.

facts.text: Opportunity drove more than 45 kilometers on Mars, setting an off-world driving record.
Spirit discovered ancient hydrothermal silica deposits while dragging a broken front wheel.

image.alt: Self-portrait by the Opportunity rover on Mars in January 2014, about three weeks before completing a decade of work

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Twin Mars Exploration Rovers Gusev and Meridiani records.
Robotic geologists Spirit and Opportunity designed for a 90-sol primary mission.
Equipped with Rock Abrasion Tools, Mössbauer spectrometers, and microscopic imagers.
Opportunity found hematite blueberries and sedimentary rocks proving ancient liquid water.
Spirit drove 7.7 km; Opportunity operated for nearly 15 years driving a marathon 45.16 km.
Spirit at Gusev (-14.5692°, 175.4729°); Opportunity at Meridiani (-1.9462°, -5.5266°).

viking-1-2.name: Viking 1 and Viking 2 Landers
viking-1-2.summary: The Viking landers were the first American spacecraft to touch down safely and operate on Mars.
viking-1-2.hook: We operated through the late 1970s and transmitted humanity first panoramic photographs of Mars.
viking-1-2.how_it_worked: Powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs) with biological test chambers and meteorology booms.
viking-1-2.science: Recorded weather cycles, analyzed soil chemistry, and observed seasonal frost forming on volcanic rocks.

facts.text: Viking 1 operated on the Martian surface for over six years (2,245 sols).
Viking 2 photographed winter frost made of water ice on Martian rocks in Utopia Planitia.

image.alt: First color image from Viking Lander 1 on the surface of Mars

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Chryse and Utopia Planitia landing telemetry recovered.
The first successful long-term operational landing probes on the Martian surface in 1976.
Equipped with gas chromatograph-mass spectrometers, seismometers, and robotic sample scoops.
Transmitted the first clear color panoramic views of red Martian soil and rocky plains.
Analyzed atmosphere composition and monitored weather across multiple Martian years.

voyager-1.name: Voyager 1 Interstellar Probe
voyager-1.summary: Voyager 1 completed historic flybys of Jupiter and Saturn before becoming the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space.
voyager-1.hook: My 3.7-meter high-gain dish still points back toward Earth from beyond the heliopause, carrying a Golden Record.
voyager-1.how_it_worked: Uses three plutonium-238 radioisotope thermoelectric generators and S/X-band transmitters communicating with NASA's Deep Space Network.
voyager-1.science: Captured the Pale Blue Dot portrait and measures plasma density, cosmic rays, and magnetic fields in the interstellar medium.

facts.text: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in August 2012, over 18 billion kilometers from the Sun.
Radio signals between Earth and Voyager 1 take more than 22 hours to travel each way at the speed of light.

image.alt: Voyager 1's "Pale Blue Dot" (2020 reprocessing): Earth appears as a tiny, softly blue speck inside a band of scattered sunlight, photographed from about 6 billion kilometers away in 1990.

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Faint X-band carrier locked via Deep Space Network calibration.
Launched in 1977 on a Grand Tour alignment that occurs once every 176 years.
Discovered active silicate volcanism on Jupiter's moon Io in 1979.
Imaged Saturn's rings and Titan's nitrogen haze in 1980 before swinging northward.
Carries a gold-plated phonograph record of Earth sounds, music, and greetings.
Over 24 billion kilometers from home and still transmitting scientific particles telemetry.

galileo.name: Galileo Jupiter Orbiter
galileo.summary: Galileo was the first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter, study the Jovian system for eight years, and deploy a probe directly into Jupiter's atmosphere.
galileo.hook: After completing 35 orbits around Jupiter, NASA commanded me into the planet to protect Europa from terrestrial contamination.
galileo.how_it_worked: Spun at 3.15 rpm for stability while a despun instrument platform kept cameras pointed accurately using low-gain antenna workarounds.
galileo.science: Revealed strong magnetic evidence for a subsurface saltwater ocean beneath Jupiter's icy moon Europa and imaged Shoemaker-Levy 9 comet impacts.

facts.text: Galileo discovered Dactyl, the first confirmed moon orbiting an asteroid (243 Ida), while en route to Jupiter.
On December 7, 1995, Galileo's atmospheric probe descended 156 kilometers into Jupiter before pressure crushed its hull.

image.alt: Galileo color view of Jupiter's icy moon Europa: a pale, cracked ice surface crossed by long reddish-brown ridges and bands.

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Jovian system orbital ephemeris and radiation log recovered.
First orbiter dedicated to an outer gas giant planet.
Overcame a stuck main high-gain antenna by compressing science data for its low-gain dish.
Survived over four times its designed Jovian radiation belt exposure.
Confirmed liquid water oceans below icy shells on Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
Deorbited into Jupiter on September 21, 2003.

near-shoemaker.name: NEAR Shoemaker
near-shoemaker.summary: NEAR Shoemaker became the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and execute a controlled landing onto its boulder-strewn surface.
near-shoemaker.hook: Engineers designed me only as an orbiter, yet five gentle hydrazine braking burns set me down intact on Asteroid 433 Eros.
near-shoemaker.how_it_worked: Conducted five planned thruster deceleration burns to touch down at roughly 1.8 meters per second onto 433 Eros despite not being originally built as a lander.
near-shoemaker.science: Mapped Eros's potato-shaped topography, gravity field, and chondritic elemental composition, even gathering close-up gamma-ray spectra on the surface.

facts.text: On February 12, 2001, NEAR Shoemaker achieved the first asteroid landing in history on 433 Eros.
Surface gravity on 433 Eros is so weak—around 0.0006 g—that an astronaut's gentle push could exceed escape velocity.

image.alt: NEAR Shoemaker mosaic of asteroid 433 Eros: an elongated, saddle-shaped gray rock covered in craters, with a large curved depression on one side.

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Micro-gravity descent trace on 433 Eros recovered.
Completed a full year orbiting a near-Earth asteroid only 34 kilometers long.
Touchdown velocity was slower than human walking speed (~1.5 to 1.8 m/s).
Continued operating its gamma-ray spectrometer on the regolith for 16 days after landing.
Resting silently on the southern edge of Himeros crater on Eros.

cassini-huygens.name: Cassini-Huygens & Titan Probe
cassini-huygens.summary: Cassini orbited Saturn for 13 years while its European-built Huygens lander executed the farthest touchdown in history onto Titan.
cassini-huygens.hook: Huygens parachuted through Titan's thick orange nitrogen haze while Cassini spent thirteen years mapping Saturn's rings and icy plumes.
cassini-huygens.how_it_worked: Huygens separated in orbit, survived a 12-G atmospheric entry over Titan under heat shields, and deployed three staged parachutes down to hydrocarbon plains.
cassini-huygens.science: Discovered geysers of water vapor erupting from Enceladus's south pole and revealed liquid methane lakes and rivers across Titan.

facts.text: Huygens achieved the most distant spacecraft landing from Earth when it touched down on Saturn's hazy moon Titan on January 14, 2005.
Cassini concluded its mission in 2017 with 22 daring Grand Finale dives threaded inside the 2,400-kilometer gap between Saturn and its rings.

image.alt: Cassini's "In Saturn's Shadow": Saturn backlit by the Sun, its dark disk ringed by glowing rings, with faint outer rings and Earth as a pale dot.

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Titan atmospheric entry & ring-plane dive logs synchronized.
Cooperative flagship partnership between NASA, ESA, and ASI.
Huygens photographed smooth water-ice cobbles carved by liquid methane rain.
Cassini sampled active hydrothermal chemistry inside Enceladus's subsurface ocean plumes.
Vaporized intentionally in Saturn's upper atmosphere on September 15, 2017.

deep-impact.name: Deep Impact (Tempel 1 Encounter)
deep-impact.summary: Deep Impact launched an autonomous copper impactor straight into the nucleus of comet Tempel 1 to expose primordial solar system material.
deep-impact.hook: My autonomous optical navigation steered a 370-kilogram copper block into a comet at 10.2 kilometers per second while my flyby craft filmed.
deep-impact.how_it_worked: The flyby bus released an autonomous 370-kilogram copper-core impactor into comet Tempel 1 at 10.2 km/s, using Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav) thruster corrections up to impact.
deep-impact.science: Vaporization plumes revealed Tempel 1 contains water ice, organic compounds, silicates, and a surprisingly fluffy porous interior structure.

facts.text: The impactor continued snapping close-up images until only 3 seconds before colliding with comet Tempel 1 on July 4, 2005.
After its primary encounter, the flyby spacecraft was repurposed as EPOXI to image comet Hartley 2 and search for exoplanets.

image.alt: Comet Tempel 1 photographed by the Deep Impact flyby spacecraft 67 seconds after the impactor struck it, with a bright burst of light and debris erupting from the nucleus.

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Tempel 1 optical impact sequence reconstructed.
Delivered the first controlled excavation into the interior of a comet nucleus.
Copper was chosen specifically so its spectral signature would not interfere with cometary chemistry.
Follow-on spacecraft Stardust-NExT returned in 2011 and imaged the 150-meter impact crater.
Flyby spacecraft remains in heliocentric orbit after contact ended in 2013.

new-horizons.name: New Horizons (Pluto-Kuiper Belt)
new-horizons.summary: New Horizons rocketed past Pluto in July 2015, transforming the distant dwarf planet from a blurry pixel smudge into a geologically active world.
new-horizons.hook: Launched at nearly 58,000 kilometers per hour, I had one unrepeatable flyby pass across Pluto's frozen heart before rushing onward into the Kuiper Belt.
new-horizons.how_it_worked: Unable to carry enough propellant to brake into orbit after a nine-year fast cruise, the spacecraft executed pre-programmed autonomous slews across Pluto's system during closest approach.
new-horizons.science: Revealed nitrogen glaciers circulating across a vast nitrogen ice plain named Sputnik Planitia across Pluto, towering water-ice mountains, and haze layers in thin nitrogen skies.

facts.text: On July 14, 2015, New Horizons swept within 12,500 kilometers of Pluto at roughly 49,600 km/h.
On January 1, 2019, it achieved the farthest planetary flyby ever performed at Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth (486958).

image.credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Southwest Research Institute
image.alt: New Horizons enhanced-color view of Pluto from July 14, 2015: a round world in pale blues, yellows and deep reds, with the bright heart-shaped plain of Sputnik Planitia.

reel_notes: Unit-7 telemetry: Pluto closest-approach optical frame buffer recovered.
Fastest spacecraft launch speed off Earth in mission history until Parker Solar Probe.
Completed the initial reconnaissance of every classical major world from Mercury to Pluto.
Because bandwidth from 4.8 billion km away is ~1-2 kilobits/sec, downlinking Pluto encounter data took 16 months.
Currently traversing deep Kuiper Belt space more than 58 AU from the Sun.
